A mountain road about 1,300 kilometres long, running from Hasan Abdal near Islamabad in Pakistan up the Indus and Hunza valleys to the Khunjerab Pass on the Chinese border, at about 4,700 metres one of the highest paved border crossings in the world. Pakistan and China built it together, from 1959 until it opened in 1979.

It follows old routes linking South Asia to Central Asia, branches of the network often called the Silk Road (see Silk Road opens). Beyond the pass, the road continues to Kashgar in Xinjiang. Building it through gorges of loose rock, with constant landslides, was dangerous work, and hundreds of Pakistani and Chinese workers died.

The road ended the isolation of the northern mountain valleys, which had been days of hard walking from the plains, and brought trade and tourism. It also gave China and Pakistan a strategic overland link. In 2010 a huge landslide at Attabad dammed the Hunza river and drowned a stretch of it. Since 2015 the highway has been rebuilt as part of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, under the Belt and Road Initiative.
